title: Realization of rationalized integral coefficients in condensed E module objects
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed field extension, and let $k$ be a field of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $\mathcal O_E$ be the valuation ring of $E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. For every separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal R_T(E)=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi]$ be the raw rationalized category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], whose integral category is [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and let $\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ and $E_T^c$ be the module-object category and coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. There is a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism
$$E_T^c\cong\bigl(V\mapsto C(|V|,E)\bigr)$$
(here $V\to T$ is an object of the small pro-etale site, $|V|$ is the entire underlying Zariski topological space of $V$, and $C(|V|,E)$ denotes continuous functions to the normed field $E$, with pointwise ring operations and restriction by precomposition), and an $E$-linear equivalence $J_T:\mathcal R_T(E)\simeq\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ induced by derived extension of scalars from the completed integral coefficient sheaf to this ring sheaf. In particular the archived criterion of stratified local finite presentation agrees, after finite refinement of the stratification if necessary, with bounded cohomology that is stratified locally free of finite rank over the continuous $E$-coefficient sheaf; every object of $\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ is isomorphic to $J_T(M)$ for an integral constructible complex $M$ viewed in $\mathcal R_T(E)$.

For every $k$-morphism $h:T\to U$ between such schemes, the ambient condensed-module functors $Lh_c^*$ and $Rh_{c,*}$ preserve $\mathcal C^c(E)$ and have natural comparison isomorphisms
$$J_TLh_{\mathrm{rat}}^*\cong Lh_c^*J_U,\qquad J_URh_{\mathrm{rat},*}\cong Rh_{c,*}J_T,$$
where the rational functors are those of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. These comparisons preserve the units and counits of the pullback/direct-image adjunctions: inserting a rational unit and then applying $J$ gives the condensed unit under the displayed comparisons, and the same holds for counits. They preserve the identity and composition isomorphisms of pullbacks. Thus the comparison obtained from pullback composition and the equality of two composite scheme morphisms corresponds to the same comparison in the condensed categories. These assertions concern categories, individual functors and their adjunction and composition structures, and impose no cartesian-square or properness hypothesis.

For a cartesian square of these schemes with arrows $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$, and with $f$ proper and any integral bounded constructible $M$, the rationalization of the specified ordered completed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] is the unit-square-counit mate for the rationalized adjunctions just described. Its image under $J_{Y'}$, conjugated by the displayed pullback and direct-image comparisons, is the restricted condensed unit-square-counit exchange of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] at $J_XM$. This is an equality of the specified transformations, not just an isomorphism between their sources and targets; no invertibility of exchange is asserted here.

proof.text: First check the finiteness hypotheses. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal. By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], a finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ is locally Noetherian; by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], separatedness and finite type make it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus $T$ is Noetherian. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] its dimension is finite. The nonzero element $\ell$ has an inverse in $k$ and hence in every local ring of $T$. The same properties hold for the locally closed strata used below: locally their rings are localizations of quotients of Noetherian rings, and their chains of irreducible closed subsets have bounded length. Their quasi-compactness follows by applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] to the open part of their closed support.

source.place: Propositions 6.6.11 and 6.8.11: checking the scheme hypotheses

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality], $E_T^c$ is $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$ and local finite presentation gives local finite freeness on each Noetherian stratum; the converse is the finite presentation of a finite free module. Thus the archived category consists of bounded complexes with stratified lisse cohomology. For $A=\mathcal O_E$, [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] supplies $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T=C(|-|,A)$ and the sheaf localization $A_T[1/\varpi]=E_T$. The canonical comparison with point pullback, including naturality for $A\to E$, is [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations]; it applies because both topological rings are totally disconnected. Consequently the composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] identify their coefficient pullbacks for every morphism. These are the actual coefficient maps. The two cited module-encoding equivalences retain underlying sheaves, coefficient actions, finite free modules and scalar restriction, so all subsequent constructions apply to the archived internal modules. The specified scalar-extension identification is [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-module-encoding-scalar-extension].

source.place: Lemmas 4.2.12, 4.2.13, 6.8.2; the cited archived coefficient and module-encoding bridges

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], an integral object has bounded stratified constructible cohomology, its cohomology sheaves and truncations remain integral objects, and its category is closed under cones. Scalar localization of module sheaves is exact: as an underlying abelian sheaf it is the filtered colimit of the sequence $M\xrightarrow{\varpi}M\xrightarrow{\varpi}\cdots$, by the usual fraction relation $m/\varpi^n=(\varpi m)/\varpi^{n+1}$. Exactness follows from the two cited colimit statements, which also show that its termwise action commutes with cohomology. On a local integral presentation, tensoring with $E_T$ gives a finite presentation over $E_T$, which is locally free by step 2. Thus $J_T^0(K)=E_T\otimes^L_{A_T}K=K[1/\varpi]$ lands in the archived category. It inverts the scalar $\varpi$; on a localized morphism $u/\varpi^n$ define $J_T(u/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}J_T^0(u)$. The fraction relation respects composition, so this defines an exact $E$-linear functor from the raw rationalized category. Scalar extension is left adjoint to restriction on sheaves: $\phi$ corresponds to $m\mapsto\phi(1\otimes m)$, with inverse $e\otimes m\mapsto e\psi(m)$, by balancing. Both functors are exact. Their termwise derived functors are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], and [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] derives this adjunction on the whole categories.

source.place: Propositions 6.6.11, 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14(2); explicit construction of its scalar-localized functor

proof.text: For integral $K,L$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-derived-hom] with $R=A_T$ and $t=\varpi$. Its Hom/coproduct-continuity hypothesis follows from [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-bounded-below-compactness] applied to a shifted common-bounded-below family: take degree-zero cohomology and use [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] to identify it with Hom into that shifted family. Direct sums of $A$-modules are exact, so this passage commutes with the sums. The copies of bounded $L$ have a common lower bound. Step 2's actual coefficient identification therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{E_T}(J_TK,J_TL[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A_T}(K,L[q])[1/\varpi]$, by $u/\varpi^n\mapsto\varpi^{-n}J_T(u)$. At $q=0$ this is the Hom formula defining [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Compatibility with identities and composition proves full faithfulness.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); telescope and Hom exactness spelled out

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-triangulated-image] to the singleton preorder, with its only category the raw rationalized integral category and its only functor $J_T$. Step 3 shows this functor is exact; step 4 shows it is full, so every arrow between image objects lifts within that same category. These are precisely the directed-image lemma's hypotheses, with identity transition functor. Its conclusion gives closure of the essential image under zero, shifts and distinguished triangles. Every lisse $E_T$-sheaf has a constructible integral model by [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice]. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] this model in degree zero is integral. Thus lisse sheaves are in the image, and the image is closed under the cone constructions used below.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 and Proposition 6.8.14(2): lattice and cone argument

proof.text: Let $F$ be a stratified lisse $E_T$-sheaf. Finite free local models are finite constant local models $E_T\otimes_E E^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration] with condensed coefficient $C(-,E)$. It gives a finite filtration with quotients $v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$, where $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow T$ is open, $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ is reduced closed, and $L_k$ has a finitely presented $E$-module local model, hence is lisse. Step 1 checks the lattice hypotheses on $S_k$, so choose the integral constructible lattice $N_k$ of [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice]. The exact functors $v_{k!}$ and $(t_k)_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] extend $N_k$ to an integral constructible sheaf on $T$: use its finite supporting stratification and the zero module on the complementary strata. The coefficient restrictions are those of step 2, and the integral characterization certifies membership. Scalar localization commutes with $v_{k!}$ because it is a left adjoint, and with $(t_k)_*$ because its filtered-colimit clause applies on the qcqs $V_k$. Thus $J(v_{k!}(t_k)_*N_k)=v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$. Induct on the finite filtration, starting with $0$. By [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4), applied to the standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] on $D(E_T)$, whose heart contains the module sheaves in degree zero, each extension is the cone of its connecting morphism between the adjacent quotient and the preceding term, with a shift. Full faithfulness lifts that morphism and the cone argument of step 5 puts the extension in the image. Hence every stratified lisse sheaf is in the image.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), stratification devissage; existing finite-model filtration tool (Stacks Tag 09Y5)

proof.text: For a bounded complex in the archived category, induct on the length of a cohomological interval $[a,b]$. If it has no nonzero cohomology, it is the zero object. Otherwise the standard truncation triangle [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] expresses it using $\tau_{\leq b-1}K$ and $H^b(K)[-b]$. The former has a shorter interval and the latter is in the image by step 6. Full faithfulness and cone closure from steps 4 and 5 give an integral model for $K$. This proves essential surjectivity and therefore the asserted $E$-linear equivalence; no idempotent completion is required.

The coefficient maps of step 2 identify ordinary module pullback with exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. The structure map $c_h:h^{-1}A_U\to A_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is this isomorphism: [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] makes the point-pullback comparison natural for the continuous quotients $A\to A/\varpi^n$, so both maps have the same components in the limit $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$. Pulling back the finite supporting stratification gives locally closed strata by [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification], and the pro-etale covers pull back by weakly etale stability [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] and fpqc covering stability [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Each local perfect $A$-complex stays the same local perfect complex with the pulled coefficient ring. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] shows the ordinary pullback is integral and already complete. The actual completion unit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is consequently an isomorphism to completed pullback; [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies its finite quotients. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] with $R=A_U$ and $t=\varpi$, using step 2's identification of $h^{-1}A_U$ with $A_T$. This gives the scalar comparison on the ordinary derived pullback; composing with the inverse completion unit gives $J_TLh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}\cong Lh_c^*J_U$. Its unit, identity and composition equations are those of the cited coherence node and of point pullback. In particular it pulls back the numerator of a local fraction and keeps its denominator.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Remark 6.8.15; comparison with the defined completed pullback

proof.text: First check that $h$ is qcqs and finite type. The inverse image of any affine open of $U$ is open in Noetherian $T$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply the same argument to the diagonal, whose source is $T$, to obtain quasi-separatedness. Clause (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], applied to $T\to U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, gives local finite type; combined with quasi-compactness this gives finite type. Now [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] and the integral characterization show that the completed integral direct image is integral. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] it agrees with the actual ambient direct image. The localization cocone of $M$ is sent by $H^qRh_*$ to a colimit cocone by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-localization-push-continuity], for every $q$: $M$ is bounded below, and step 2 identifies its coefficients with the continuous integral ones. Its telescope uses $\ell$; [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] gives $E=A[1/\ell]$, so its vertex and zeroth leg are the same scalar extension and unit as $M[1/\varpi]$ in step 2. Hence the canonical scalar comparison $(Rh_*M)[1/\varpi]\to Rh_{c,*}(M[1/\varpi])$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. The restriction comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identifies its target and action with the actual field-coefficient direct image, not just an abstract group. This gives $J_URh_{\mathrm{rat},*}\cong Rh_{c,*}J_T$. Essential surjectivity from step 7 then proves preservation of the condensed constructible subcategory.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; Remark 6.8.15; bounded-below qcqs continuity used for localization

proof.text: Use the integral pullback/direct-image adjunction and localize its Hom bijections. The functor and natural-transformation formulas in [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] preserve compositions and identities, so the localized units and counits still satisfy the two triangle identities. The comparisons of steps 8 and 9 are an adjoint pair of comparisons: the direct-image comparison is the adjunct of the scalar-extension pullback comparison followed by the integral counit, because both send a fraction $m/\varpi^n$ by the same counit map divided by $\varpi^n$. This is the module scalar-extension adjunction explicitly derived in step 3, followed by the scheme module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For coefficient restriction, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] applies with $R_T=A_T$, $S_T=E_T$ and their identified point-pullback coefficient maps from step 2; its adjunct equation gives exactly this compatibility on restrictions. Consequently its unit equation is $J(\eta_N)=\eta^c_{JN}$ and its counit equation is $J(\epsilon_M)=\epsilon^c_{JM}$ after inserting these comparisons. These equations can also be checked by adjunction: both sides of the unit equation correspond to the identity of the pullback object and both sides of the counit equation correspond to the identity of the direct-image object. This proves the asserted adjunction compatibility. Step 8 proves composition compatibility, so its square-composition comparison also agrees.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; explicit adjunction check for the scalar-extension comparisons

proof.text: For the specified exchange, fix compatible etale-origin witnesses provided by integral membership. In [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization], set $M=Lg^*Rf_*K$, $N=Rf'_*Lg'^*K$ and write $e:M\to N$ for the ordinary integral mate. That node gives the strict equality $v'_\bullet=H'\mathcal R(e)H^{-1}$. Let $\delta_M:M\to R\lim\mathcal R(M)$ and $\delta_N:N\to R\lim\mathcal R(N)$ be the quotient-tower completion units. They are isomorphisms: steps 8 and 9 make $M,N$ integral. Naturality gives $R\lim\mathcal R(e)\,\delta_M=\delta_Ne$. Write $\gamma_g:M\to Lg^*_{\rm comp}Rf_*K$ and $\gamma_{g'}:Lg'^*K\to Lg'^*_{\rm comp}K$ for step 8's units. Under the source identification in [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], its map $s$ is $(R\lim H)\delta_M\gamma_g^{-1}$. Indeed $H$ is the pulled-back projection-formula comparison, and both maps insert the strict reduction unit. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], its target comparison $c$ satisfies $c\,Rf'_*\gamma_{g'}=(R\lim H')\delta_N$: this is exactly its specified completion-unit formula and the projection formula for $Lg'^*K$. All equalities are of strict-tower-derived maps before taking the derived limit; no faithfulness of level evaluation is used.

source.place: Additional specified-map comparison: strict reduction units, projection-formula normalization and direct-image limit comparison

proof.text:
Substitute step 11's identities into the specified ordered composite. Functoriality of $R\lim$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ex}^{\rm comp}
&=c^{-1}(R\lim H')(R\lim\mathcal R(e))(R\lim H)^{-1}s\\
&=(Rf'_*\gamma_{g'})\delta_N^{-1}(R\lim\mathcal R(e))\delta_M\gamma_g^{-1}\\
&=(Rf'_*\gamma_{g'})e\gamma_g^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the completed exchange is the ordinary mate with the actual completion-unit comparisons inserted. Localize this equality by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Step 10 and the composition compatibility of step 8 identify its three ordered mate factors with the rational unit, square comparison and counit. Applying $J$ and those same compatibility equations identifies them with the condensed unit, square comparison and counit of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Their ordered composite is exactly its specified exchange. This proves equality of the specified transformations without asserting or using invertibility of exchange.
